newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes mixed after thin deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes mixed after thin deal.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices finished mixed after drifting narrowly in featureless dealing, with an easier close in Tokyo dampening sentiment.

Dealers said the market lacked strong consumer demand as buyers continued to wait for attractive prices. Producers are also holding back their stocks in anticipation of slow inflow because of the wintering period.

Scattered consumers from Asia were seen in the afternoon but most activities were on hand-to-mouth basis, they said. Trading houses offered SMR 20 at 296 cents a kg, SMR CV at 360.50, SMR L at 340.50, SMR 5 at 302.50, SMR 10 at 297.50 and latex at 240.
"We really expect the Europeans to make some fresh inquiries for forward positions although the consumers have covered their near-term commitments."
At the close, March RSS 1 buyer gained one cent to 304 cents ($1.22) a kg but March SMR 20 buyer was down a cent at 295.50 cents.
The INRO five-day moving average was 232.42 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 5 against 232.19 on March 4. The daily indicator price was 233.03 against 232.75.
